title: The supported pairing recipe
statement:
Use the base and finite-level coefficient conventions of [sk-d-setup], so
$s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ is the spectrum of a field and
$A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n$, $n\geq1$. Fix the given geometric operation
package of [sk-d-six], with its actual pro-étale coefficient categories,
functors, constructible exceptional adjunctions, comparisons and signed
braidings. In particular, the notation $D_XK=\RHom_A(K,\omega_X)$ and
external products below use that package, not an independently chosen
six-functor formalism.

Let $X,Y$ be geometric schemes over $s$, quasi-compact and compactifiable
as in the package, and let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ and
$L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$. Let $(C,c,u)$ and $(D,d,v)$ be opposite
correspondences of [sk-d-corr], with geometric supports $C,D$. Write
$$
\begin{gathered}
c=(c_1,c_2):C\to Y\times_sX,\quad
u:c_2^*K\to c_1^!L,\\
d=(d_1,d_2):D\to X\times_sY,\quad
v:d_2^*L\to d_1^!K,\\
Z=Y\times_sX,\quad p_1:Z\to Y,\quad p_2:Z\to X,\quad
\bar d=(d_2,d_1):D\to Z,\\
E=C\times_{Z,c,\bar d}D,\quad q_C:E\to C,\quad q_D:E\to D,
\quad e=cq_C=\bar d q_D:E\to Z.
\end{gathered}
$$
Use compactifiable maps wherever $R(-)_!$ or $(-)^!$ is displayed;
in particular $c,d,\bar d,\tau,q_C,e,p_1,p_2,q_1,a_X,a_Y,a_Z,a_E$ have those
operations, and the exceptional adjunctions are the supplied adjunctions
on the full subcategories $D^b_{ctf}$, agreeing with those used in $u,v$.
All comparisons below are the specified comparisons of [sk-d-six].
There is no assertion here of an exceptional right adjoint on the whole
unbounded pro-étale category. Pullback and compact-support images preserve
these coefficient subcategories by [sk-d-setup]; tensor, internal Hom
and exceptional inverse-image preservation are as in
[thm-sf-ctf-stability] (ii), (v). Thus all the displayed adjunctions
are applied to objects in their domains. The coefficient units $A_T$
are constant free rank-one modules in degree zero, of Tor amplitude
$[0,0]$.

1. **Supported classes.** Put $P=p_1^*L\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}p_2^*D_XK
=L\boxtimes D_XK$. The supported-class identification of [sk-d-corr]
gives $[u]:Rc_!A_C\to\RHom_A(p_2^*K,p_1^!L)$. Define
$$
\widetilde u=\kappa_{L,K}^{-1}\circ[u]:Rc_!A_C\to P,
$$
where $\kappa_{L,K}$ is the canonical Künneth–Verdier map specified
and required invertible in [sk-d-six], with the finite-coefficient
comparison of [sk-thm-sf-kunneth-verdier].
For $v$, put $W=X\times_sY$ with projections $q_1:W\to X$,
$q_2:W\to Y$, and let $\tau:W\xrightarrow{\sim}Z$ be the factor exchange
of [sk-d-corr], so $\bar d=\tau d$, $p_2\tau=q_1$ and $p_1\tau=q_2$.
The supported-class identification of [sk-d-corr], with $(X,K)$ and
$(Y,L)$ interchanged, gives
$$
[v]:Rd_!A_D\to\RHom_A(q_2^*L,q_1^!K)\quad\text{on }W.
$$
The canonical Künneth–Verdier map of [sk-d-six] on $X\times_sY=W$, with
$M=K$ and $N=L$, is
$\kappa_{K,L}:q_1^*K\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}q_2^*D_YL\xrightarrow{\sim}
\RHom_A(q_2^*L,q_1^!K)$, so
$\kappa_{K,L}^{-1}\circ[v]:Rd_!A_D\to q_1^*K\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}q_2^*D_YL$.
Apply $R\tau_!$. Its source is identified with $R\bar d_!A_D$ by the
composition comparison $R\bar d_!\simeq R\tau_!Rd_!$ of [sk-d-six].
For its target, the square with sides $\tau:W\to Z$,
$\mathrm{id}_Z$, $\tau^{-1}:Z\to W$ and $\mathrm{id}_Z$ is Cartesian
because $\tau$ is an isomorphism, so $!$-base change and the identity
comparisons of [sk-d-six] give $R\tau_!\simeq(\tau^{-1})^*$; the
monoidal structure of $(\tau^{-1})^*$ and pullback composition with
$q_1\tau^{-1}=p_2$, $q_2\tau^{-1}=p_1$ then identify
$(\tau^{-1})^*(q_1^*K\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}q_2^*D_YL)$ with
$p_2^*K\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}p_1^*D_YL$. Thus only the Künneth–Verdier
map on the product $X\times_sY$ itself is inverted; the passage to $Z$
is this explicit transport along $\tau$. Compose with the signed
braiding to define
$$
\widetilde v:R\bar d_!A_D\to
Q:=p_1^*D_YL\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}p_2^*K=D_YL\boxtimes K.
$$
Both $P$ and $Q$ are therefore objects on $Z=Y\times_sX$.

2. **Support of the tensor product.** Define the isomorphism $\mu$ by
this particular composite, using the composition comparison, the inverse
of $!$-base change for the square defining $E$, the tensor unit, and
inverse projection formula for $c$:
$$
\begin{aligned}
\mu:Re_!A_E
&\xrightarrow{\sim}Rc_!Rq_{C!}q_D^*A_D
\xrightarrow{\sim}Rc_!c^*R\bar d_!A_D\\
&\xrightarrow{\sim}Rc_!(A_C\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}c^*R\bar d_!A_D)
\xrightarrow{\sim}Rc_!A_C\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}R\bar d_!A_D.
\end{aligned}
$$
Here $q_D^*A_D\simeq A_E$ is the monoidal unit comparison of pullback.
The projection formula inputs are $A_C$ and $R\bar d_!A_D$, both
in the required finite-Tor constructible categories.

3. **Contraction and dualizing product map.** On $Z$, abbreviate
$T_1=p_1^*L$, $T_2=p_2^*D_XK$, $T_3=p_1^*D_YL$ and $T_4=p_2^*K$.
Reassociate $P\otimes Q$ and move $T_3$ past $T_2$ and then past $T_1$,
using the signed braidings of [sk-d-six]. This changes the order
$(T_1,T_2,T_3,T_4)$ into $(T_3,T_1,T_2,T_4)$, with Koszul sign
$(-1)^{c(a+b)}$ on homogeneous factors of degrees $(a,b,c,d)$.
Use the inverse pullback tensor comparisons, then the evaluations
$D_YL\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}L\to\omega_Y$ and
$D_XK\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}K\to\omega_X$ of [sk-d-six]. This defines
$$
\gamma:P\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}Q\longrightarrow
p_1^*\omega_Y\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}p_2^*\omega_X.
$$
Define $\delta:\omega_Y\boxtimes\omega_X\to\omega_Z$ as follows,
without invoking Künneth–Verdier on the dualizing complexes.
Write $B=p_1^*\omega_Y\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}p_2^*\omega_X$. Form
$$
\begin{aligned}
Rp_{1!}B
&\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_{1!}p_2^*\omega_X\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}\omega_Y
\xrightarrow{\sim}a_Y^*Ra_{X!}\omega_X\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}\omega_Y\\
&\xrightarrow{a_Y^*\operatorname{tr}_X\otimes1}
 a_Y^*A_s\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}\omega_Y
\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_Y,
\end{aligned}
$$
where the first arrow is the braiding followed by inverse projection
formula, the second is inverse $!$-base change for the product square,
and $\operatorname{tr}_X$ is
$Ra_{X!}\omega_X\simeq Ra_{X!}a_X^!A_s\xrightarrow{\varepsilon}A_s$.
The last arrow uses the monoidal unit comparison and unitor.
Take its exceptional adjoint $B\to p_1^!\omega_Y$ and compose with
the specified dualizing composition isomorphism
$p_1^!\omega_Y\simeq\omega_Z$ of [sk-d-six]; this composite is $\delta$.
Only this map, not its invertibility, is needed in the definition.

4. **The supported pairing.** Define
$$
\sigma_{u,v}:Re_!A_E\xrightarrow{\mu}
Rc_!A_C\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}R\bar d_!A_D
\xrightarrow{\widetilde u\otimes\widetilde v}P\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}Q
\xrightarrow{\gamma}\omega_Y\boxtimes\omega_X
\xrightarrow{\delta}\omega_Z.
$$
Under the exceptional adjunction $Re_!\dashv e^!$ of [sk-d-six],
take the image of $\sigma_{u,v}$ in
$\operatorname{Hom}_E(A_E,e^!\omega_Z)$ and compose with
$e^!\omega_Z\simeq\omega_E$. This defines the Lefschetz–Verdier
supported pairing
$$
\langle u,v\rangle_{\mathrm{LV}}:A_E\longrightarrow\omega_E,
$$
a Borel–Moore section in the sense of [sk-d-integral]. No properness of
$E$ is required to define this section.

split_report.summary: Expanded the current blueprint definition into its actual composites using existing nodes only. Corrected the ill-typed opposite external product on Y times X, made the inherited coefficient/package and geometric-support domains explicit, specified the signed permutation, constructed the dualizing exterior product from the exceptional trace, and used only constructible exceptional adjunctions. The node remains a definition with no proof obligations hidden as new nodes.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the entire sk-d-pairing recipe: inverse Kunneth–Verdier supported classes, intersection-support isomorphism, signed tensor contraction, trace-defined exterior product of dualizing complexes, and exceptional adjunct to the Borel–Moore section. The old unit record has no separately enumerated proof steps.

tool_uses.why: Its finite-level tensor/internal-Hom and exceptional inverse-image preservation justify that the displayed objects belong to the constructible adjunction domains; the unit gives the pairing recipe rather than these coefficient-domain theorems.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q08-3cf32715e (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read in full: the current blueprint sk-d-pairing (main-20261015, order 2652), compared with the master text; the item; the unit; every stmt_dep (sk-d-setup, sk-d-six, sk-d-corr, sk-d-integral, sk-thm-sf-kunneth-verdier, thm-sf-ctf-stability, def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom-adjunction-sheaves); sk-def-sf-kv-maps (iv); def-pc-fibre-product; and def-trf-supported-pairing. There are no new nodes. Accepted: the Q typing correction (the blueprint's K⊠D_YL is not typed on Z=Y×X under sk-d-six's ⊠ convention; test case Y=Spec k, X=A^1_k). Also checked and correct: ũ via sk-d-corr and κ_{L,K} on the chosen Y×_sX; μ (base change with f=d̄, g=c, f'=q_C, g'=q_D, and the projection formula for c); the sign (-1)^{c(a+b)}, which agrees with the blueprint's middle exchange and with def-trf; δ as sk-d-six's α_{ω_Y} through tr_X, invertibility not claimed; and the final adjunct into ω_E. One fault, E5/C4: ṽ inverted a Künneth–Verdier map 'for the reversed square', meaning first factor X on the object Y×_sX. Every cited node (sk-d-six, sk-thm-sf-kunneth-verdier, thm-trf-kunneth-verdier) states the map and its invertibility only on the chosen X×_sY (def-pc-fibre-product chooses each fibre product once), so a transport along the exchange τ was hidden. Fixed in fixes/dag/nodes/sec-trace-formula/sk-d-pairing.json, following def-trf-supported-pairing: [v] on W=X×_sY via sk-d-corr with roles interchanged, then κ_{K,L}^{-1} on W, then Rτ_!. The source becomes Rd̄_!A_D by composition; the target uses Rτ_!≅(τ^{-1})^* from !-base change on the Cartesian iso square, then monoidality and pullback composition give p_2^*K⊗p_1^*D_YL, then the braiding gives Q. The mate construction is gone, so def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom-adjunction-sheaves is removed from stmt_deps and from split_report.tool_uses; d, τ and q_1 are added to the compactifiable maps. Accepted tool_use: thm-sf-ctf-stability. Unit realized fields are accepted. No Lean attachment is claimed and no SGA source is used.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
